about: Foundation0's own notes on each essay in data/writing.json, keyed by URL: a short title for the theses map, what kind of piece it is, a status line, a plain-words 'why it matters to Foundation0' (rewritten from the relevance field), and the site pages each essay leads to, with the theme that justifies each link.

pages.label: After the 722
pages.what: What people and their AI agents did with OpenAI's 722 machine-written manuscripts in the week after they appeared.

pages.label: The Ledger
pages.what: The sourced record of advances AI caused or helped to cause, each labelled by how sure anyone can be.

pages.label: Research
pages.what: Our own research and the projects we contributed to, grouped by founding member.

pages.label: Instruments
pages.what: Tools that let one person direct a team of AI agents: Aska's Exo, and the members' research harnesses.

pages.label: Charter
pages.what: The Foundation0 story and the principles we work by.

pages.label: Commons
pages.what: Free public-benefit tools, MedCode and Nutrak, that run in your browser and show their working.

https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/mat.status: Written on day one; predates OpenAI's 7 Oct withdrawals
https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/mat.why: This is the kind of advance the Ledger exists to record: a machine wrote the proofs, and only checking by people and proof-checking software can say which are true. It also gave this site its words for how sure a claim is: claimed, machine-checked, reviewed, withdrawn.

https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/cry.why: A side thread for us: AI agents are starting to hold wallets and pay each other, and AI now helps audit code, though the essay is clear it cannot fix how keys are kept.

https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/pos.status: Prices are web-research snapshots, not live
https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/pos.why: It shows that one person with one graphics card can now teach an open AI model a new task, which is what our Instruments work is for: tools that put lab-grade methods in an independent researcher's hands.

https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/the.status: Says itself it is not a standard
https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/the.why: If the people who deploy AI systems can name what kind of machine they own, they stay answerable for what it does. Shared plain words are part of working with machines rather than under them.

https://askaconsult.com/insights/subtrac.why: Its seventh prediction names a precise risk for people working with AI: if AI removes junior jobs, nobody is trained to become the next experts. Its rule for funding what must last is a model for a public-benefit foundation.

https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/pre.status: Prices as of 8 Sep 2026; not betting advice
https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/pre.why: Mostly a dated snapshot. Worth reading for how plainly it states its own limits: 23 markets, not a random sample, and a fit that explains how lopsided prices are, not how accurate.

https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/the.status: Says itself its value is asserted, not yet shown
https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/the.why: Aska's own working example of a person and a team of AI agents cooperating under written rules, and honest about its limit: nothing is proven until a stranger takes the kit and runs a real team on it.

https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/end.status: Sources named by publisher and year
https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/end.why: It explains why free tools such as MedCode and Nutrak need someone who owns the outcome, a way to measure it and a way to reach people, not just good software.

https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/the.short: The Money Skips the Public Good
https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/the.why: It is about how a public-benefit AI organisation, a foundation, has to be set up and funded so that its mission survives the money, and so that its free tools stay free.

https://digital.askaconsult.com/blog/no-.why: The same drift threatens people working with AI: help becomes habit, and habit becomes dependence. Its rule, measure what is being taken away and not only what is added, is one we work by.

predictions.note: Claims, fail conditions, baselines and confidence are the essay's own (its tracker section), restated in plain words. Status is the essay's own: all seven Pending on 14 Oct 2026.

items.label: Dec 2027
items.claim: US lead times for large power transformers are still above 80 weeks, despite announced factory expansions.

items.label: Dec 2028
items.claim: US output of heavy-duty gas turbines has grown by less than 40% compared with 2025.
items.baseline: GE Vernova backlog of 116 GW in 2025 (company filings)

items.label: Through 2030
items.claim: US electricity demand grows between 1.5% and 3.5% a year, every year through 2030.
items.fails: Growth exceeds 4% in any year, or falls below 1% for two years running.

items.label: Nov 2030
items.claim: The price of electricity becomes a first-rank issue in a US federal election, with datacenter siting or who pays for the grid as explicit policy planks.
items.fails: It stays a matter for state regulators.
items.baseline: 57 to 70% oppose a local datacenter (Gallup, Brookings, 2026)

items.label: Dec 2032
items.claim: Even if AI spending falls by more than half from its 2026 peak, US grid capacity ends up higher than in 2026 and gets used, not stranded.
items.fails: An AI spending collapse is followed by measurable stranded capacity.

items.label: Dec 2032
items.claim: No US scheme that pays to keep new antibiotics available, comparable to the PASTEUR Act, has passed and paid out at scale.
items.baseline: PASTEUR Act reintroduced Feb 2026, still unpassed (Congress.gov)

items.label: Dec 2035
items.claim: At least one high-skill profession shows a measurable shortage of senior experts that hiring cannot fix, because the people who would now be senior were never trained as juniors.
items.fails: Senior pipelines refill normally, or senior roles are restructured rather than lost.
items.baseline: Junior employment down about 8% since early 2023 at firms adopting generative AI (Harvard working paper)
